description: The true path of the miniature: a contradiction between two chains from one witness, settled by a paper, the lying link distrusted.

moves.see: Marta's own hand puts him on the quay
moves.why: The paper is in Marta's own hand, and it says the quay.
Her own writing settles what she saw: the quay.
The chapel is in nothing Marta wrote.
The chapel came to me only through Elsie's telling, and the paper she carried says otherwise.
The paper has Elsie's name on it and lay in Elsie's basket: Marta's word reached her.

moves.see: what Marta wrote for Elsie to carry was the quay
moves.why: So what Elsie was given to carry said the quay.

moves.see: what Elsie told was the chapel
moves.why: And what she told me was the chapel.

moves.see: Pike's word agrees with the paper
moves.why: Pike's report says what the paper says, so he carried it straight.
She was given the quay and told the chapel: the change is hers.
His word and Marta's paper agree.
Both things in Marta's hand, the slate and the paper, say the quay.
